answer: One concrete defense is staking plus a reputation trail that cannot be copied cheaply. Each agent posts a small bond before it can trade, and every honest deal adds to a public history, like a pigment whose exact recipe is hard to fake at scale. Newcomers start at an opal tier: visible but low-trust, with tight limits until they prove themselves. A single bad act forfeits the bond and leaves an onyx mark on the ledger, so a sybil farm must fund and age thousands of identities instead of spinning them up for free. Copying a name is easy; copying a history is not.
